findings.finding: Q4 guide arithmetic from the company's own statements points at or slightly above the ~$575-579M Q4 bar: Tower said it will cross a $1B SiPho annualized run rate in Q4 2026 (>= $250M/quarter vs $170M in Q2) with wafer-start capacity ~3x Q2 by year-end, customer advances jumped from $27.5M to $321M in H1 (deferred revenue/advances, current $25.6M->$176.0M, long-term $1.9M->$145.4M), and since then NewPhotonics entered high-volume shipment on PH18DA (6-K 2026-09-17) and Semtech paid for dedicated SiGe capacity (6-K 2026-10-13); against that, RF mobile (12% of revenue) was -35.5% y/y and expected down all 2026, so the non-SiPho ~$235M base must hold flat for a guide near $580M+.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Verified bmo release-day closes (Yahoo daily bars): Q3'25 2025-11-10 +16.7% (84.07->98.10), Q4'25 2026-02-11 -1.6% (Intel corridor withdrawal disclosed, Q1 seasonal guide), Q1'26 2026-05-13 +22.6% (220.83->270.77, raised outlook, $1.3B 2027 SiPho contracts), Q2'26 2026-08-04 +2.2% (234.32->239.53, $520M Q3 guide above street). The guide/SiPho line has driven the two big up moves.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has de-rated 32% in 20 sessions and 49% from the high on sector selling with no company news; if the market had priced the company's own $1B Q4 SiPho run rate as delivered, the stock would not be trading at the 10-30 level with 20 vol points of put skew. The Q4 consensus was set in August and has not visibly moved since (Zacks SCR $575M).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue should land at or just above the $520M guide midpoint (bar $521.7-522.1M): Tower's last two quarters printed $414M vs a $412M guide and $460M vs a $455M guide, i.e. +0.5% to +1.1% over midpoint, and Q2 utilization was 83% with Fabs 2/3/9 at 80-85%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been small (Q4'25 beat by $0.4M; Q2'26 by ~$5M) and the stock's moves came from the guide, not the quarter: Q2'26's $5M beat with the guide closed +2.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it sits inside the company's own guided range and consensus sits on the midpoint. Filed small because a midpoint-plus print is the expected outcome; a print below ~$510M would be the surprise and nothing points to it.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 guide $412M from https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20512846 (Q1 release, 2026-05-13, revenue $414M); utilization from Zacks SCR https://s27.q4cdn.com/906368049/files/News/2026/Zacks_SCR_Research_08042026_TSEM_Thompson.pdf. Shares the Q2 6-K with the guide finding.

findings.finding: AXT, an indium phosphide substrate supplier, reported on 2026-10-29 record Q3 revenue of $73.4M (+54% q/q) vs ~$66M guided, said InP demand is exceptionally strong and it has more than quadrupled its 2026 InP opportunity, with capacity to ~$60M/quarter by year-end; Tower flagged InP supply as a constraint on its heterogeneously integrated SiPho (PH18DA) ramp on its Q1 call, so supply growth at the substrate level eases one named risk to the Q4 run-rate target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Tower print turned on InP supply; the Q1'26 call that raised the constraint closed +22.6% on the overall outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: It printed the day before a 13% sector-driven fall in TSEM, so whatever read-through existed was swamped; if it had been priced the stock would have held up relative to the chip complex on 10-29/10-30 rather than falling with it (TSEM -2.9% on 10-29, -13.5% on 10-30).
findings.independence: Proxy: AXT does not name Tower as a customer. Tower's own InP constraint statement: Q1 2026 summary https://www.gurufocus.com/stock/TSEM/transcripts/8856515 via search; Tower Q1 release https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20512846.

findings.finding: AI networking counterparties that spoke after Tower's 08-04 guide all lifted: Celestica (10-27) printed Q3 revenue ~$5.83B, +83% y/y, above its $5.25-5.55B guide and raised FY2026 to ~$21B with ten 1.6T programs; Alphabet (10-28) raised FY26 capex to $195-205B and signalled 2027 capex above $300B. Both feed 800G/1.6T optical transceiver demand that Tower's SiPho and SiGe serve.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TSEM rose +6.7% on 10-26 and +5.8% on 10-27 around Celestica's print, then gave it all back on 10-29/10-30, so the read-through has been bought once and erased by the sector.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: TSEM rallied on it and then lost it in the 10-30 chip rout. What remains unpriced is whether Tower converts it into a Q4 guide; that is carried by the guide finding, so this is sized small.

findings.finding: Intel warned on 2026-10-29/30 that PC weakness from AI-driven component (memory) costs could last through 1H27, triggering a chip rout (Intel ~-25 to -29%); Tower's consumer-exposed lines - RF mobile 12%, power management 14%, sensors and displays 12% of Q2 revenue, together ~38% - face that same component-cost squeeze on PC and handset builds, a risk to the non-SiPho base in the Q4 guide. Net of the SiPho/SiGe ramp (RF infrastructure 49% and growing 142% y/y) the effect is a modest drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4'25 (2026-02-11) was the one guided quarter with a non-SiPho headwind disclosed (RF mobile -15%, Intel corridor withdrawn) and it closed -1.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector already marked down on 10-30, TSEM included (-13.5%), so much of this is in the entry price; the residual is the specific Q4 guide on the consumer lines, which Tower has not addressed since the Intel warning.
